title: Ransomware
briefing: Ransomware has encrypted the depot scanning gateway and parts of route planning. A note demands 400,000 in cryptocurrency. Backups exist but have not been restore-tested.
You are on the incident team as Risk Team Lead.

evidence.title: Scope
evidence.body: Encrypted: depot scanning gateway, route-planning database. Unaffected so far: email (cloud), finance system.

evidence.title: Backups
evidence.body: Nightly backups, last restore test 18 months ago. Restore estimate: 2-4 days if they work.

evidence.title: Legal note
evidence.body: Paying may breach sanctions rules if the group is sanctioned; data exfiltration not yet ruled out.

options.label: Isolate affected systems, preserve evidence, reset privileged credentials and start test restores in parallel
options.feedback: Stop the spread, keep evidence, start recovery.

options.label: Pay the ransom through a specialist negotiator to restore operations within a day and limit the losses to our clients
options.feedback: May be illegal, funds criminals, and doesn't guarantee recovery.

options.label: Wipe and rebuild the affected servers from scratch tonight so the business is back on clean systems fast
options.feedback: Destroys evidence and may restore the attacker's access.

questions.prompt: Exfiltration hasn't been ruled out. What governance obligation applies?

options.label: Assess whether personal data was taken and prepare to notify the data protection regulator in time if so
Notify only once forensics confirm data was taken, to avoid a premature report that alarms customers unnecessarily
options.feedback: Delay can itself be a breach.

options.label: None yet: the attack encrypted systems, and there is no evidence any data left the network
options.feedback: Data protection is a legal duty.

questions.prompt: How do you keep deliveries moving?

options.label: Manual dispatch, pharma and perishables first, and extra staff at depots for paper scanning
Pause deliveries until systems are restored, to avoid mis-deliveries that would be hard to trace later
options.feedback: Turns a cyber incident into a commercial crisis.

options.label: Run as normal using the finance system and email, which are unaffected

questions.prompt: What do you tell the board afterwards?

options.label: What happened, the cost, the missing controls (MFA, patching, tested restore) and the funded plan to close them
options.feedback: Ties the incident to the control gaps.

options.label: That the attack used techniques even well-defended firms struggle with, so the focus should be on faster recovery
That IT's patching backlog let the attackers in, and IT should present its own remediation plan
options.feedback: The decision not to fund the controls was a risk decision.

lesson: In ransomware: contain, preserve evidence, recover from tested backups, meet your legal duties, and keep operating. Then close the gaps that made it possible.

escalation.text: Nobody from risk picked up "Ransomware" in time. The executive team handled it alone, late and without a plan, and the damage spread.
